relationships.subject: acute nociception
relationships.evidence_quote: acute noxious stimuli, including capsaicin-induced inflammatory pain, acetic acid-induced visceral pain, and incision-induced surgical pain, significantly delayed recovery from sevoflurane anesthesia in male mice

relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: acute noxious stimuli, induced by the injection of capsaicin under sevoflurane anesthesia, increased c-Fos expression and activity in the GABAergic neurons of the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray

relationships.subject: vlPAG GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: the vlPAG<sup>GABA</sup> neurons regulated the recovery from anesthesia through the inhibition of ventral tegmental area dopaminergic neuronal activity

relationships.subject: vlPAG GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Specific reactivation of capsaicin-activated vlPAG<sup>GABA</sup> neurons mimicked the effect of capsaicin and its chemogenetic inhibition prevented the delayed recovery from anesthesia induced by capsaicin.

key_findings: Acute (but not chronic SNI) nociception delays emergence from sevoflurane anesthesia in mice, preventable by peripheral analgesics.
Capsaicin activates vlPAG GABAergic neurons, which delay anesthesia recovery by inhibiting VTA dopaminergic neurons and reducing dopamine release and D1-like receptor activation.
